props.title: Death Spa
props.initialSlug: Killer gym equipment terrorizes fitness fanatics

sections.content: Death Spa represents peak 1980s high-concept horror, blending aerobics culture with supernatural revenge in gloriously absurd fashion. It's part of a specific wave of health club horror films like Killer Workout (1987) and Perfect (1985), capitalizing on the decade's fitness obsession. The film's outrageous mix of haunted health equipment, possessed computers, and neon-drenched murder scenes perfectly captures the excess and technological anxieties of late 80s genre cinema.

sections.content: The film's technological horror elements connect it to other 80s gems like Chopping Mall (1986) and Evilspeak (1981), where computers become conduits for supernatural mayhem. Director Michael Fischa embraces both body horror and slasher conventions, creating memorable death scenes involving exercise equipment turned deadly. The film's commitment to practical effects, including some impressive gore work by special effects artist Dan Frye, exemplifies the hands-on approach of 80s horror filmmaking.

What sets Death Spa apart is its commitment to the aesthetic excess of the era. The neon lighting, spandex costumes, and electronic score by Peter Kaye create a time capsule of 80s health club culture. This pairs perfectly with similar genre entries like Terror Train (1980) and The Burning (1981), where confined spaces become hunting grounds for elaborate kills. SUBHEAD: The Tech-Horror Connection

movies.title: Demons 2
movies.slug: Evil forces invade an apartment complex through television signals

sections.content: The film's fusion of supernatural horror with technology anxiety reflects broader cultural fears about automation and computer dependence. Similar themes appear in films like Demon Seed (1977) and Electric Dreams (1984), though Death Spa takes a more gleefully exploitative approach. The health club's automated systems becoming instruments of death presage later tech-horror films like Ghost in the Machine (1993).
